narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, excited, slightly outraged comedy explainer narrator. Punchy, sarcastic, brisk delivery with no long pauses.

clerk.instruct: Polite, overly fancy jewellery-store clerk, quietly proud of the price.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You just bought a shiny new razor for ten dollars. What a bargain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: First shave? Smooth as a dolphin. You feel like a movie star.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two weeks later, the blade tugs your face like tiny pliers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go buy refills, and they're locked in a glass case.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Right next to the perfume, the phones and the fancy watches.

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.text: Eight refills? That comes to forty dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Four times the price of the razor. The handle was just the bait.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside each refill, the steel costs well under five cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The plastic adds another three to five cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All the materials? Under thirty cents. The shelf price? Five dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's fifteen to twenty times what the stuff is worth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In nineteen oh-four, a razor maker patented the throwaway blade.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sell the handle once. Sell the blades forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And to keep you paying, they keep adding blades.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two blades in the early seventies. Seven blades by twenty seventeen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At this rate, your next razor comes with a tiny lawnmower.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No wonder the store guards them like diamonds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Back at the shelf, a new guy grabs a shiny ten dollar razor.
